extracted.intended_audience: International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authorities (patent examiners), receiving Offices, and patent applicants/practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting international search and preliminary examination under the PCT, covering priority claims, classification, rectification of obvious mistakes (Rule 91), exclusions from search/examination, and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of priority right for novelty/inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: The priority right assumes importance if subject matter relevant to the determination of novelty or inventive step (non-obviousness) of the claimed invention: (i) has been disclosed within the meaning of Rule 64.1 on or after the priority date claimed and before the international filing date; or (ii) forms part of the content of an application or patent within the meaning of Rule 64.3 that was published on or after that date but filed earlier than the international filing date or claimed the priority of an earlier application filed prior to the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases the examiner must satisfy himself that the priority date(s) claimed may be accorded to the appropriate parts of the international application and, where appropriate, consider the validity of any priority date claimed under Rule 64.3 (see also Rule 70.10). When considering priority date, bear in mind matters in paragraphs 6.03–6.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing priority: documents taken as a whole
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish a priority date, it is sufficient that the documents of the previous application taken as a whole specifically disclose the elements of the invention, even if not all elements are found among the claims in the previous application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description and any claims or drawings of the previous application should be considered as a whole, except do not take into account subject matter found solely in that part of the description referring to prior art or in an explicit disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific disclosure requirement for priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure in the priority document must be specific; mere implication or broad/general reference to elements is insufficient for priority to a detailed embodiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact correspondence is not required; it is enough that, on a reasonable assessment, there is in substance a disclosure of the combination of all the important elements of the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for entitlement to priority (equivalent to Article 34(2)(b) test)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the priority date to be allowed, the subject matter of the claim must be explicitly or inherently disclosed in the priority document, including any features implicit to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit disclosure examples: a claim to apparatus with 'releasable fastening means' is entitled to priority from a disclosure showing a nut and bolt, spring catch, or toggle latch provided the general concept is implicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant date when priority tests not satisfied
rubrics_metrics.description: If the tests for priority entitlement are not satisfied for a particular earlier application, the relevant date of the claim will be either the priority date of the earliest application that does satisfy the tests or, in the absence of such, the international filing date of the international application itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements for claiming priority (Form PCT/RO/101 and Rule 4.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant wishing to claim priority must state this on the request (Form PCT/RO/101) giving particulars of the previous filing as specified in Rule 4.10; later correction of priority claims (including addition or deletion of entire claims) is permitted under Rule 26bis within time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prescribed form of declaration under Rule 4.10(a) includes indicating: (i) date of earlier filing; (ii) number of earlier application; (iii) where national application, country; (iv) where regional, the regional authority; (v) where international, the receiving Office. For regional applications the applicant may indicate one or more Paris Convention countries for which that earlier application was filed. If a regional application includes at least one country not party to Paris Convention/WTO, the priority claim must indicate at least one country party to the Convention or a WTO Member for which that earlier application was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and timing of priority documents (16-month rule and alternatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit the priority document to the International Bureau or the receiving Office within 16 months of the priority date unless already filed with the receiving Office together with the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives: (i) where the priority document is issued by the receiving Office, request the receiving Office to prepare and transmit it; (ii) request the IB before international publication to obtain the priority document from a digital library if available per Administrative Instructions. A priority document received by the IB after 16 months will be considered received on the last day of the 16‑month limit if received before international publication. If the receiving Office transmits or is requested to transmit before the 16-month limit, the time limit is complied with irrespective of when the IB actually receives the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and correction/addition of priority claims (Rule 26bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indications concerning a priority claim, if not made in the request, must be furnished to the IB or receiving Office within 16 months of the priority date or within 16 months from a changed priority date, whichever period expires first; a notice correcting or adding a priority claim may be submitted until expiration of four months from the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction of a priority claim may include correction or addition of any indication referred to in Rule 4.10. If time limit under Rule 26bis.1 has expired an applicant may request the IB to publish information concerning the matter prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date, subject to payment of a special fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner access to priority document and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner needs a copy of the priority document, the IB supplies it unless the IB has not yet received it. If the priority document is not in an ISA/IPEA language, the examiner may invite the applicant to furnish a translation within two months of the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any written opinion established while there is still time to furnish the priority document or translation may proceed as if the priority had been validly claimed; however, if the document or translation is not timely furnished, further written opinion or international preliminary examination report may proceed as if the priority had not been claimed. No designated Office may disregard a priority claim before giving the applicant an opportunity to furnish the priority document within a reasonable time, and no DO may disregard the claim if the document is available from a digital library per Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification requirement under IPC (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every international application must be classified by the International Searching Authority according to the International Patent Classification system (IPC). The classification of the international application is determined by the ISA and symbols are applied according to current IPC rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPC Guide is available via WIPO. If multiple classification symbols are required, all are assigned in accordance with the IPC Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification based on disclosure as filed (not probable amended content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification is determined without taking into consideration the probable content of the international application after any amendment; it should relate to the disclosure in the published international application, i.e., the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner's understanding of the invention or content as filed alters significantly as a result of the search (e.g., due to prior art found or clarification of obscurities), the classification should be amended accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended classification when ISR published separately
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international search report is not available in time for publication with the international application and is published separately, and the examiner finds it necessary to amend the original classification for reasons such as those in 7.04, the amended classification is included in the international search report, indicated by adding the word 'amended' that it replaces the one published on the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendment should not be made unless the examiner is quite certain it is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification when scope is obscure
rubrics_metrics.description: When the scope of the invention is not clear, classification should be based on what appears to be the invention insofar as it can be understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may be necessary to amend classification later if obscurities are removed by the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of all claimed inventions despite lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: All claimed inventions must be fully classified, whether or not there is lack of unity of invention, since all are disclosed in the published international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each invention claimed is classified as set out in the classification paragraphs (7.02–7.06).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of applications excluded from international search
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISA finds that an international application relates to subject matter it is not required to search or that a meaningful search cannot be carried out, classification is nevertheless made, to the extent possible, and communicated to the IB for publication purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of obvious mistakes (Rule 91) — general principle and time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Mistakes due to something other than that which was obviously intended (e.g., linguistic, spelling errors) may be rectified if a request for rectification is submitted within 26 months from the priority date and the necessary criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mistake must be 'obvious' to the competent authority: (i) that something else was intended than what appears; and (ii) that nothing else could have been intended than the proposed rectification. It must be clearly apparent to the competent authority that a mistake was made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-fold test for rectification of obvious mistake
rubrics_metrics.description: The test for rectification is two-fold: (i) recognition that there was indeed a mistake; and (ii) assessment whether the proposed rectification was the only meaning which could have been intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For corrections to description, claims, or drawings the finding must be made only on the basis of the description, claims and drawings, without reliance on extrinsic documents. Contents of priority documents should not be taken into account for considering whether mistakes are obvious and rectifiable. Mistakes in chemical or mathematical formulae would not generally be rectifiable unless the correct formula was common knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent authority to decide rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent authority (receiving Office, International Bureau, ISA or IPEA depending on circumstances) determines whether an alleged mistake is obvious and thus rectifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 91.1(b) allocation: (i) mistake in request or its correction — receiving Office; (ii) mistake in description/claims/drawings or their correction — ISA (unless IPEA competent); (iii) mistake in description/claims/drawings or amendment under Article 19/34 where demand for IPE has been made and not withdrawn and IPE start date passed — IPEA; (iv) mistake in other documents submitted to RO/ISA/IPEA/IB — that Office/Authority/Bureau as applicable. If an authority receives a request it is not competent to authorize, it transmits it to the appropriate authority and informs the applicant; it may instead inform the applicant to send it to the competent authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable date for applying rectification test
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicable date at which to determine whether a request for rectification should be approved is: (i) where the alleged mistake is in a part of the international application as filed (including the request) — the international filing date; (ii) where the alleged mistake is in a document other than the international application as filed — the date on which the document containing the alleged mistake was received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge that came into being after the applicable date may not be used to rectify the mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistakes that cannot be rectified under Rule 91
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Rule 91.1(g) a mistake shall not be rectified if: (i) the mistake lies in the omission of one or more entire elements of the international application (request, description, claims, drawings or abstract) or one or more entire sheets; (ii) the mistake is in the abstract; (iii) the mistake is in an amendment under Article 19, unless the IPEA is competent as described; (iv) the mistake is in a priority claim or in a notice correcting/adding a priority claim where rectification would cause a change in the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions for providing a missing element or sheet to the receiving Office are provided in Rules 20.3–20.8. An applicant may propose modifications to the abstract under Rule 38.3. Changes to the priority claim, other than changes in priority date, may be made under either Rule 91 or Rule 26bis. Corrections/additions affecting priority date may only be effected in accordance with Rule 26bis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional invitation to request rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: If an International Authority discovers what appears to be an obvious mistake in the international application or any other document submitted by the applicant, it may invite the applicant to submit a request for rectification to the authority competent to authorize the rectification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although permitted, such invitations are not expected to be issued since any mistake rectifiable under Rule 91 should not impede establishing the search report or affect the substance of any written opinion or international preliminary examination report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and processing of a request for rectification (forms and time)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rectification must be submitted to the competent authority within 26 months from the priority date. It must specify the mistake and the proposed rectification and may contain a brief explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the ISA is competent and receives such a request it considers whether rectifiable, marks documents per Section 511, completes Form PCT/ISA/217 and forwards the request and form to the receiving Office, the IB and the applicant. During international preliminary examination an applicant may request rectification of obvious mistakes of his own volition; the examiner may also note obvious mistakes. Where rectification is authorized or refused by IPEA, the Authority notifies the applicant using Form PCT/IPEA/412 and forwards copies to the IB and applicant, marking as per Section 607.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of authorization of rectification on international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorized rectification under Rule 91.1 must be taken into account by the ISA for the purpose of the international search (including ISR and written opinion) unless the rectification is authorized by, or notified to, the ISA after it has begun to draw up the ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISR, if possible, indicates whether the rectification has been taken into account. If the ISR fails to indicate this, the ISA notifies the IB, and the IB proceeds as provided in the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication consequences of rectification authorization or refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the competent authority refuses to authorize a rectification, upon the applicant's request the IB publishes the request for rectification, the reasons for refusal and any brief comments by the applicant, if possible together with the international application, provided the request for publication is submitted within 2 months from the date of refusal and subject to payment of a special fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request for publication was received after completion of technical preparations for publication, the request and reasons/comments are published promptly after receipt and the front page is republished. If authorization was received by the IB before completion of technical preparations, the international publication includes the rectification. If authorization is received after completion, a statement reflecting all rectifications is published together with the sheets containing the rectifications or replacement sheets and the letter furnished under Rule 91.2; the front page is republished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of an authorized rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where rectification of an obvious mistake has been authorized, it is effective: (i) for a mistake in the international application as filed — from the international filing date; (ii) for a mistake in a document other than the international application as filed — from the date on which the document was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus rectification in the application as filed is effective retroactively from filing date; rectification in other documents is effective from submission date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim and scope of 'meaningful search' and limits on absence of search
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of the ISA and IPEA is to issue international search reports and international preliminary reports on patentability that are as complete as possible. 'Meaningful search' should be read to include a search that within reason is complete enough to determine whether the claimed invention complies with substantive requirements (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability) and/or sufficiency, support and clarity requirements of Articles 5 and 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A finding of 'no meaningful search' should be limited to exceptional situations in which no search at all is possible for a particular claim (for example, where description, claims, or drawings are totally unclear). To the extent description/claims/drawings can be sufficiently understood, a search should be performed, recognizing non-compliance may affect the extent of the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject matter from international search/examination (Rules 39 and 67)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 39 (and Rule 67 for IPEA) specifies certain subject matter an ISA/IPEA is not required to search or examine; while such subject matter may be excluded, there is no requirement it be excluded and practice varies by Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any restriction to search or examination should be accompanied by a reasoned explanation in the written opinion or international preliminary examination report. Whether an Authority searches/examines certain listed subject matter depends on its policy and Agreements with the IB; these choices are set forth in Annexes to Agreements between Authorities and the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and mathematical theories: exclusion rule and practical application/technical character
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere presence of scientific or mathematical theories in claims does not immediately exclude claims from search or preliminary examination. If, when viewing claims as a whole, the theories are applied or implemented to produce a practical application or to have technical character, search and preliminary examination is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the physical theory of semi-conductivity (pure theory) would be excluded, whereas a new semiconductor device or manufacturing process would be searched. A shortcut method of division may be excluded, but a calculating machine designed to operate accordingly would be searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant/animal varieties and essentially biological processes (exclusion nuances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant and animal varieties may be excluded from search, but transgenic plants, genetically modified non-human animals and methods of making such inventions would be searched and examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a process is 'essentially biological' is a question of degree depending on the extent of technical intervention by man; significant technical intervention (e.g., application of growth-stimulating substance) would not be excluded. Microbiological processes and products thereof are not excluded; the term covers industrial processes using microorganisms and processes for producing microorganisms (e.g., by genetic engineering). Products of microbiological processes (including plasmids and viruses) may be searched and claimed; propagation of such products is to be construed as a microbiological process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schemes, business methods, mental acts, playing games (abstract items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schemes, rules or methods of doing business, performing purely mental acts or playing games are examples of items of an abstract or intellectual character that may be excluded from search/examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the abstract character, not classification or particular art, that determines exclusion. The appendix to the chapter contains guidance where divergent practices exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for treatment/diagnostic methods on the human or animal body (exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy, and diagnostic methods practiced on the human or animal body, are subject matter on which an Authority is not required to carry out international search or preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search and preliminary examination should be conducted for surgical/therapeutic/diagnostic instruments or apparatus for use in such methods, and for new products (particularly substances or compositions) for use in these methods of treatment or diagnosis.
